name: An Isolated Passive Blocker Forms a Peripheral Active Cell
statement: In the passive-owner normal form, let $d\in R$. There are a passive coordinate $z$, a nonempty set $W\subseteq Y\setminus N_L(d)$, and an ample family $C\subseteq D\cap Q_W(d)$ containing $d$ and $d^{\oplus W}$ such that $(d^{\oplus W})^{\oplus z}\in K$. Moreover $C\cap S_z=\{d^{\oplus W}\}$, and the conditioning of $A$ to $Q_{W\cup\{z\}}(d)$ is the peripheral expansion $C\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{(d^{\oplus W})^{\oplus z}\}$ with singleton duplicated site. The cell $C$ lies in the unique minimal active carrier of $d$.
proof: Localize the failure of $K\cup\{d\}$ to an antipodal pair $\{d,h\}$ on a face $Q_T(d)$. An interval-exit path inside $D\cap[d,h]$ ends with an edge to $h$. That edge must use a passive coordinate $z$; an active exit would put another member of $K$ in the isolated face. Thus $W=T\setminus\{z\}$ is nonempty and $h^{\oplus z}=d^{\oplus W}$. Isolation also gives $W\cap N_L(d)=\varnothing$. Conditioning $A$ on the active $W$-face produces an ample family $C$ on the residual side and only the mate of $d^{\oplus W}$ on the opposite passive side, proving the peripheral-expansion and unique-owner assertions. Agreement with $d$ on $N_L(d)$ places all of $C$ in its unique minimal carrier.
